domain_restrictions: For each i in 1..d, w_i is a positive integer
S is graded with degree of x_i equal to w_i
Each g_i is homogeneous in S with respect to this grading
The quotient ring S/(g_1,...,g_d) has finite dimension as a k-vector space
The quotient S/(g_1,...,g_{i-1}) uses the ideal generated by g_1 through g_{i-1}
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: Assume k is a field, d is a nonnegative integer, and S is the weighted graded polynomial ring on d variables over k with deg(x_i)=w_i where each w_i is a positive integer. For any homogeneous elements g_1,...,g_d in S, if the k-vector space S modulo the ideal generated by g_1 through g_d is finite-dimensional, then for each i from 1 to d, the natural image of g_i in the quotient S modulo the ideal generated by g_1 through g_{i-1} is not a zero-divisor. Equivalently, the sequence g_1,...,g_d is a homogeneous regular sequence with respect to the same grading.
quantifier_order: Let d be a nonnegative integer
For each i in 1..d, let w_i be a positive integer
Let S be k[x_1,...,x_d] with grading deg(x_i)=w_i
For all choices of homogeneous elements g_1,...,g_d in S, if S/(g_1,...,g_d) is finite-dimensional over k, then for each i in 1..d the image of g_i in S/(g_1,...,g_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor

witness_dependencies: No existential witnesses are introduced; the statement is universal in g_1,...,g_d and concludes a property for each index i

statement_nl: Let k be a field, let d be a nonnegative integer, let w_1,...,w_d be positive integers, and let S = k[x_1,...,x_d] be graded by deg(x_i)=w_i. If g_1,...,g_d are homogeneous elements of S and S/(g_1,...,g_d) is finite-dimensional over k, then for each i the image of g_i in S/(g_1,...,g_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor. Equivalently, g_1,...,g_d is a homogeneous regular sequence.
